hook.text: Americans return $816 billion in goods yearly. Every return travels backward through the supply chain.

buildup.text: Reverse logistics handles returns, repairs, recycling, and disposal—moving goods from customer back to origin.

discovery.text: It includes inspection, sorting, refurbishing, reselling, and responsibly disposing of items that can't be reused.

twist.text: Returns cost retailers 60% of the item's original price on average. Free returns are not free for the company.

climax.text: Companies like Patagonia turned reverse logistics into a brand asset by reselling used gear at lower prices.

punchline.text: Products go forward. Returns go back. Both need a plan.
